formatNotes: Qualification: worldwide Open, then top 5 men and 5 women from each of 8 Regionals (40 per division). No mid-competition cuts for individuals. 15 scored events on a 100-point-per-event scale, except the three short Sunday-morning tests (Handstand Walk, Suicide Sprint, The Plow), which were worth 50 points each (1,350 points max). To mark the 10th CrossFit Games, the first three events were held off-site at The Ranch in Aromas, California (site of the 2007-2009 Games); athletes were flown north to Aromas on Wednesday, July 20. In the Ranch Deadlift Ladder athletes lifted in reverse order of current standings.
yearSummary: The 10th CrossFit Games opened with a surprise return to The Ranch in Aromas, where a 7-km trail run, a 20-bar deadlift ladder, and a hillside chipper recalled the Games' origins before competition moved back to the StubHub Center in Carson. Programming leaned heavily on new implements: the sand-filled Snail, the Plow, the 150/100-lb D-ball, and the SkiErg all debuted, while the pegboard returned in the final event, Redemption, after wrecking the field in 2015. Murph also returned from 2015, this time run on a Friday morning and with mandated partitioning after the previous year's heat problems. Mathew Fraser won just one event, the opening Ranch Trail Run, but took 2nd in five others (Events 3, 5, 6, 7 and 15) and never sat worse than 2nd overall after Event 3, winning his first title with 1,096 points and a 197-point margin over Ben Smith, the largest in Games history to that point; rookie Brent Fikowski won 4 events and finished 4th, with Patrick Vellner 3rd and Rookie of the Year. The women's race was a season-long duel: Katrín Davíðsdóttir won the Handstand Walk and The Plow on Sunday morning, collapsing past the finish line of the latter, to overhaul Tia-Clair Toomey and repeat as champion by 11 points, 984 to 973, with Sara Sigmundsdóttir 3rd.

events.name: Ranch Trail Run
events.description:
For time:
7-km trail run through the hills of The Ranch in Aromas, California.
Same course and format for men and women.
events.notes: First event of the surprise Ranch day in Aromas marking the 10th Games. Fraser opened his campaign with the event win.

events.name: Ranch Deadlift Ladder
events.description:
Deadlift ladder, similar to the 2009 Games deadlift ladder:
1 deadlift every 30 seconds through a series of 20 barbells of increasing weight; score is the heaviest successful lift.
Men's bars (lb): 425-435-445-455-465-475-485-495-505-515-525-535-545-555-565-575-585-595-605-615.
Women's bars (lb): 275-285-295-305-315-325-335-345-355-365-370-375-380-385-390-395-400-405-410-415.
Athletes lifted in reverse order of the standings.
events.notes: Sam Dancer was the only man to clear all 20 bars (615 lb); Alex Vigneault was 2nd at 595 and Lucas Parker 3rd at 575. Brooke Wells cleared the women's ladder with a 415-lb PR. Ties at the same weight shared points (e.g., Travis Williams and Spencer Hendel both at 565 lb). Conflict: Wikipedia's table shows roughly 20-lb increments over 11 bars, but the official workout page lists 20 bars (men in 10-lb steps, women in 10-lb then 5-lb steps), which is corroborated by the 595- and 575-lb podium lifts.

events.name: Ranch Mini Chipper
events.description:
For time:
50 wall-ball shots
25 med-ball GHD sit-ups
Hill sprint carrying the med ball
Men use a 30-lb medicine ball, women a 20-lb medicine ball, for all three pieces.
events.notes: Final event of the Aromas Ranch day, finishing with a sprint up the hillside. The official card does not list a wall-ball target height or sprint distance; Wikipedia reports targets of roughly 10 ft (men) and 9 ft (women). The 30/20-lb ball is heavier than the standard 20/14-lb wall ball.

events.name: Ocean Swim
events.description:
For time:
500-m ocean swim.
Athletes started on the beach, swam out and around two buoys, and finished back on the beach.
events.notes: Held at 9 a.m. at Redondo Beach (per Wikipedia), the only individual event on Thursday. Khan Porter was 2nd for the men at 7:03.17.

events.name: Murph
events.description:
For time, wearing a weight vest (20 lb men / 14 lb women):
1-mile run
then 5 rounds of:
20 pull-ups
40 push-ups
60 squats
then 1-mile run.
Unlike 2015, the middle work was required to be partitioned into the 5 rounds.
Time cap: 55 minutes.
events.notes: Controversial repeat of the 2015 event, after athletes suffered heat injuries in 2015 (notably Annie Thorisdottir); in 2016 it was moved to Friday morning and the gymnastics work was partitioned. Josh Bridges won Murph at the Games for the second straight year.

events.name: Squat Clean Pyramid
events.description:
For time, with rolling deadlines per bar (athletes could move ahead of the deadlines):
10 squat cleans, 245 lb / 165 lb (by 2:00)
8 squat cleans, 265 lb / 180 lb (by 4:00)
6 squat cleans, 285 lb / 195 lb (by 6:00)
4 squat cleans, 305 lb / 205 lb (by 8:00)
2 squat cleans, 325 lb / 215 lb (by 11:00)
Time cap: 11 minutes.
events.notes: Friday afternoon in the tennis stadium; 30 total reps across five progressively heavier stations. Athletes not finished with a station by its deadline were scored by reps completed.

events.name: Double DT
events.description:
10 rounds for time of:
12 deadlifts
9 hang power cleans
6 push jerks
Men 155 lb, women 105 lb (one barbell throughout).
Double the 5 rounds of the hero WOD DT.
Time cap: 15 minutes.
events.notes: Friday night closer in the tennis stadium. DT is a hero workout honoring USAF SSgt Timothy P. Davis; here it was doubled to 10 rounds at the standard load. Davidsdottir's win was a key swing in the women's title race.

events.name: Climbing Snail
events.description:
3 rounds for time of:
500-m berm run (up and along the stadium berm)
2 rope ascents
40-ft Snail push (500-lb Snail men / 400-lb Snail women)
2 rope ascents
Per contemporaneous reports the third round ended after the Snail push, with no final pair of rope ascents (10 ascents total).
The bottom of the ropes hung above head height, so each ascent began with a jump and legless pulls.
Time cap: 21 minutes.
events.notes: Debut of the Snail, a barrel-shaped implement partially filled with sand so the load constantly shifted to the bottom as it rolled. Conflict: the official card lists rope ascents after the Snail push in every round; Wikipedia and event recaps say the final round had none.

events.name: The Separator
events.description:
For time.
Men:
12 ring handstand push-ups, 15 back squats (225 lb), 20 burpees
9 ring handstand push-ups, 18 front squats (205 lb), 20 burpees
6 ring handstand push-ups, 21 overhead squats (185 lb), 20 burpees
Women:
15 back squats (165 lb), 20 burpees, 6 ring handstand push-ups
18 front squats (145 lb), 20 burpees, 4 ring handstand push-ups
21 overhead squats (125 lb), 20 burpees, 2 ring handstand push-ups
Barbells taken from the ground.
Time cap: 16 minutes.
events.notes: Saturday night in the tennis stadium. Men's and women's sequences differ: men start each round with ring handstand push-ups, women finish each round with them at lower reps. Per Wikipedia this was only the second time handstand push-ups on rings featured at the Games.

events.description:
For time:
40 box jumps (30-inch box men / 24-inch box women)
20 D-ball cleans (150 lb men / 100 lb women), taken over the shoulder
Time cap: 5 minutes.
events.notes: Short all-out sprint closing Saturday, contested in the same session as The Separator. Debut of the heavy D-ball (sand-filled medicine ball) at the Games. Conflict: the official card says box jumps; Wikipedia describes the reps as box jump overs at the same heights.

events.name: Handstand Walk
events.description:
For time:
280-ft handstand walk on the stadium floor.
Worth a maximum of 50 points (half value).
events.notes: First of three 50-point Sunday-morning tests on the same 280-ft course. Davidsdottir was the only athlete in either division to walk the full 280 ft unbroken, and her 1:33.68 was faster than every man; Kari Pearce finished less than a second behind her.

events.name: Suicide Sprint
events.description:
For time:
840-ft shuttle sprint on the same 280-ft course as the Handstand Walk:
run one-third of the way down and back,
then two-thirds of the way down and back,
then sprint the full length to the finish line.
Worth a maximum of 50 points (half value).
events.notes: Rookie Roy Gamboa (35th overall) took the men's event; CrossFit reported the average male time as 47.68 seconds. Mat Fraser was 2nd at :44.11.

events.name: The Plow
events.description:
For time:
560-ft plow drag (down and back on the 280-ft course).
Men's plow 235 lb, women's plow 190 lb.
Worth a maximum of 50 points (half value).
events.notes: Debut of the Plow. Davidsdottir staved off a late charge from Sam Briggs, collapsed past the finish line and had to be helped off the field; the win moved her past Toomey into the overall lead she kept to the end.

events.name: Rope Chipper
events.description:
For time:
200-m SkiErg
50 double-unders (men) / 40 double-unders (women)
200-m row
50 / 40 double-unders
0.4-mile Assault AirBike
50 / 40 double-unders
200-m row
50 / 40 double-unders
200-m SkiErg
90-ft hand-over-hand sled pull (310 lb men / 220 lb women)
Time cap: 11 minutes.
events.notes: Every station involved a rope or cable: SkiErg cords, jump ropes, rower chain and a rope sled pull. Games debut of the Concept2 SkiErg (the Assault bike had debuted in 2015). Some recaps report weighted jump ropes were used for the double-unders. Fikowski's 4th event win of the week; women's winner Anna Tunnicliffe is an Olympic sailing gold medalist.

events.name: Redemption
events.description:
For time:
3 pegboard ascents
21 thrusters (135 lb men / 85 lb women)
2 pegboard ascents
15 thrusters
1 pegboard ascent
9 thrusters
Time cap: 10 minutes.
events.notes: Final event, named for the pegboard's 2015 debut when much of the field could not complete a single ascent. Rookies won both divisions: Carchedi (5:37.75) beat Fraser (5:56.00) by 18.25 seconds, and Johnson won for the women; per the official leaderboard exactly 10 women (7:31.34 to 9:48.19) finished under the 10-minute cap, with the rest scored CAP+. Fraser's 2nd place sealed the largest winning margin in Games history to that point.
